name: Hot chocolate
caffeine: A little caffeine from the cocoa solids, far less than coffee; do not offer it as caffeine free.

house.ask: Not printed on the menus: ask at lineup whether hot chocolate is available, for children and for adults, and whether it is made from cocoa, chocolate or a mix.

what: Chocolate melted into hot milk, or cocoa powder whisked in with sugar. Melted chocolate keeps its cocoa butter, so the cup is richer and less sweet; cocoa powder has most of that fat removed, needs sugar and can clump. Many boxed hot chocolate mixes are cocoa. Spain makes it thick enough to dip a churro.
taste: Warm, sweet and chocolatey, with real body when made from chocolate; cocoa is lighter and sweeter. Bitterness follows the chocolate's percentage.

steps: For the thick Spanish style, whisk a little cornstarch into the cold milk first.
Heat the milk, stirring, until it steams, or thickens if starched; a cooked milk flavour suits this drink.
Whisk in the chocolate off the heat until smooth and glossy.
For cocoa instead, whisk powder and sugar to a paste in a splash of milk, then add the hot milk.
make.ratio: Spanish thick style: 1 part chocolate to 2 parts milk
make.dose: Thick style: 200 g dark chocolate, 400 ml milk, 1 tsp cornstarch
make.temp: Milk steaming; cocoa butter melts near 93F (34C)

serve: Bring it at once in a warmed mug on a saucer with a spoon, stirred as it leaves, since chocolate sinks. Cream or a dusting only if the house does them; for a child, ask whether warm rather than hot.
story: Cacao is a tree of the Americas; the oldest known trace of its use, about 5,300 years old, is on pottery from the Ecuadorian Amazon, and the smooth bar came only in the nineteenth century. Madrid takes it thick with churros, and Colombia makes it with water or milk.
guest: Hot chocolate is chocolate melted into hot milk, rich and smooth. Let me check with the bar whether we can make one tonight.
watch: Never promise it: confirm at lineup first.
Grit or clumps mean cocoa dumped straight in: whisk it smooth in a little milk first.
Dairy or allergy questions go to the service note and the kitchen.

recall.prompt: How is hot chocolate made, and how does it differ from cocoa?
recall.answer: Chopped chocolate whisked into steaming milk until glossy, served in a warmed mug. Chocolate keeps its cocoa butter, so it is richer and less sweet than cocoa, which has most fat removed and needs sugar.

quiz.q: Why is hot chocolate made from a chocolate bar richer than cocoa?
options: Its cocoa is more finely ground
quiz.explain: A bar keeps its cocoa butter, which gives body; cocoa powder has most of that fat removed.

quiz.q: What thickens the Spanish chocolate served with churros?
quiz.explain: Dark chocolate is melted into milk thickened with a little cornstarch, so it coats a spoon.

quiz.q: Why can hot chocolate take hotter milk than a latte?
options: It wants a cooked milk flavour
Melted chocolate cools the milk down
Cocoa butter stops the milk scalding
quiz.explain: Hot chocolate, like masala chai, wants a cooked milk flavour and reads thin without it.
